subject: Audit request: temporary log-eviction exemption + cross-border transfer plan
messages:
From: Nora Fisk <nora.fisk@meditek.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: security@meditek.com, procurement@meditek.com
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary log-eviction exemption + transfer note for DPA review

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As part of our security review ahead of our board sign-off, a couple of items popped up we need to reconcile with your DPA and operations team:

1) Backup purge timing: if we trigger a customer-initiated data deletion, what is the maximum window before backups and long-tail snapshots are purged? We need the timeline in writing for our data retention schedule.
2) Log eviction exception: for a scoped forensic hold (e.g., user-level legal request), can Redwood grant a temporary log-eviction exemption so logs are kept for 90 days beyond standard TTL?
3) Cross-border transfer note: several backups are landlocked in us-east today — we need to understand if any routed subprocessor transfers could move EU-origin data out of region during retention/rollback.

Could you send the operational runbook or a short playbook and any DPA amendment language we should expect? Ideally something we can show our legal/security and procurement teams.

Appreciate quick turnaround — our procurement deadline is June 10.

Best,
Nora Fisk
VP, Security & Compliance | Meditek

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Nora Fisk <nora.fisk@meditek.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary log-eviction exemption + transfer note for DPA review

Hi Nora — thanks for outlining this so clearly. High level answers inline, and I'll follow up with more detailed attachments this afternoon:

1) Backup purge timing: our default snapshot/backup purge window is 30 days post-deletion for standard plans; for Dedicated/Private customers we support configurable purge windows up to 180 days via an agreed-off annex.
2) Log eviction exception: we can support scoped exceptions with an "eviction hold" flag that prevents automated TTL eviction for a defined window (we typically handle 30–90 days). That requires an audit trail and an approval workflow; we log a circuit-breaker and an automatic rollback trigger.
3) Cross-border transfer: our VPC/private deployments keep storage region-scoped by default; hosted backups may be stored in a region specific to the account. We do not proactively transfer EU-origin data to non-EU regions without a customer-approved subprocessor or an explicit data transfer addendum.

I'm attaching a draft runbook and a redline of the DPA language we propose for the temporary eviction exemption. Kimberly and Karthik — can you confirm the evidence we would provide (logs, signed approval, ticket ids) and whether the 90-day hold is acceptable from procurement/legal?

Next steps:
- I will attach the runbook and a backup-purge timeline spreadsheet.
- Kimberly will provide suggested DPA amendment text for the eviction exception.
- Karthik will confirm subprocessor transfer controls and whether we need a cross-border data flow memo.

Thanks — aiming to have a single doc for Meditek legal by Monday (June 1).

— Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Senior Manager, Security Partnerships | Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Tessa / team — quick notes for the draft:

- Evidence package we can provide: (1) audit log export with signed timestamp, (2) approval ticket ID (internal JIRA or customer-signed DocuSign), (3) snapshot manifest showing retention TTL, (4) hash of preserved logs for integrity.
- Legal prefers the hold to be expressed as: "Customer may request a Temporary Eviction Exemption (TEE) for specific accounts or objects; Redwood will implement the TEE upon verification and will provide an evidence package within 5 business days."
- We should make the maximum hold duration configurable in the DPA annex: default 30 days, up to 90 days with exec sign-off. Anything beyond 90 days requires a procurement-level SOW.

I've attached a DPA redline (meditek_dpa_redline_v2.pdf) and a short runbook draft. Laura — can you confirm operational SLA for evidence delivery?

kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Legal Operations | Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 12:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary log-eviction exemption + transfer note for DPA review

Couple of engineering constraints and mitigations:

- Eviction hold implementation: we maintain a per-account eviction label that prevents TTL compaction for KV/append logs. It does introduce additional storage cost; we will include an incremental storage estimate in the spreadsheet.
- Rollback/circuit-breaker: if the hold is applied and we see anomalous growth, automated alerts trigger a throttled eviction path and send an ops escalation to the customer PO and Redwood on-call. We can add a soft-throttle to prevent unbounded cost.
- Cross-border snapshot routing: hosted backups are region-aware; however, some archived replicas are placed in a cross-region object store for redundancy. We can restrict MI/archival replicas to stay in the original region for Meditek with a subprocessor routing policy. That needs to be baked into the DPA addendum (list of allowed subprocessor regions).

I'll update the runbook with operational alarms, cost-impact knobs, and the rollback playbook.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Product Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: temporary log-eviction exemption + transfer note for DPA review

Hi Nora — attaching the runbook and DPA redline as discussed. Short summary:

- Backup purge timeline (hosted): default 30 days after deletion; can be extended to 180 days under an annex. See spreadsheet: redwood-backup-purge-timeline-connector.xlsx
- Temporary Eviction Exemption (TEE): customer-requested, implemented after verification. Default hold 30 days; can be extended to 90 days with exec approval. Evidence package delivered within 5 business days.
- Circuit-breaker & rollback: automatic throttles will engage if retention growth exceeds thresholds; rollback path requires a customer acknowledgement ticket and will be logged.
- Cross-border subprocessor routing: we will include an explicit subprocessor-region allowance for Meditek in the DPA addendum; no transfers out of EU for EU-origin backups without prior written consent.

Can you confirm that the 5-business-day evidence SLA and the exec-approval step for >90 days are acceptable? If so, we'll produce a final DPA amendment for procurement and a short operational playbook for your security team.

Thanks,
— Tessa
(attachments: meditek_dpa_redline_v2.pdf, redwood-backup-purge-timeline-connector.xlsx, eviction-exemption-runbook-draft.docx)
